catalog_quote: § 280. Auch im Dalmatischen bleibt der Wortakzent auf derselben Silbe wie im (Vulgär)- latein. Vom Silben- und Satzakzente kann man hier nichts Bestimintes sagen: nur werden einige Fälle angeführt, die woll auf besondere Verhältnisse deuten. Auch die Geschichte der Quantität ist bemerkenswert, aber leider ebenso dunkel. § 281. Veglia. Hervorzuheben ist hier die Enklisis bei ndune = nox ... und bei tuta-su = tata suus. ... new_statements.quote: We have no information about intonation or syllable structure, but we may at least surmise that these too were — at least in Udaina's speech — like those of the local Italo-Romance dialects. Nor is there any evidence for synchronic length distinctions. Word-stress is usually oxytonic or paroxytonic, many oxytones having arisen, historically, through the extensive deletion of word-final unstressed vowels; the proparoxytones tend to be loanwords from Italo-Romance or Slavonic.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is on the final or the penultimate syllable of the word, inherited from the Latin/Romance position: many final-stressed words arose by apocope of final unstressed vowels; antepenultimate stress occurs mainly in Italo-Romance or Slavonic loanwords. No synchronic rule predicts final vs. penult, so the placement is lexically fixed (Romance-type), not phonologically fixed.
new_statements.exceptions: Proparoxytones (antepenultimate stress), mostly loanwords from Italo-Romance or Slavonic.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened material describes Vegliote (veljotski), the Krk/Veglia variety as recorded by Bartoli (1906) from the last speaker Tuone Udaina (Antonio Udina); Hadlich 1998 (p. 26) and Swiggers 1998 (pp. 55-57) both stress that this idiolect is heavily interfered with by Venetian and Croatian. Nothing opened describes Ragusan or other Dalmatian varieties.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote confirmed verbatim in the held Bartoli 1906 scanned at the stated sections/pages. Bartoli is the primary reference grammar of an extinct language recorded from its last speaker; nothing later can supersede it on first-hand data. The modern authoritative synthesis (Maiden 2020, open AM downloaded to describes stress as oxytonic or paroxytonic with proparoxytones mostly loans and gives no positional/weight rule, which is consistent with the lexical coding and with the record's the secondary-stress rule about disfavoured proparoxytones. Ive 1886 (downloaded) is silent on a synchronic rule. Remaining unheld items (Hadlich 1965/1998, Swiggers 1998) could add an explicit 'stress is phonemic' statement but are unlikely to change the classification. no reclassification or identity issue.
